vra:descriptionSet.vra:display: The Birkat al-Mawz oasis settlement was developed east of the mouth of Wādī al-Mu‘aydin as it emerges from the foothills. It is a relative ‘new town’ by Omani settlement standards, having developed during the Ya’ariba imamate in the seventeenth century as a result of an agreement of collaboration between the imamate state and the dominant tribal confederation of the region, the Banī Riyām. A similar agreement was drawn up with the ‘Abriyīn to develop the oasis of Al Ḩamrā’ further west. Bayt al-Rudaydah, the isolated fortified dwelling – and the local seat of the Ya’āribah – guarded the access up the wadi and controlled the main source of water for the oasis. The Ya’āribah helped develop the main falaj (pl. aflāj) system for Birkat al-Mawz, Falaj al Khatmeen, now inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage Site (WHS) list, along with four other Omani aflāj systems. To maximise arable land use and to prevent flood damage two settlements quarters are located on the low foothills along the northern edge of the oasis. The oldest of these, Ḩārat as-Saybani, has a watchtower at its apex and two falaj channels passing through it, which evidently became incorporated through successive expansions of the quarter downhill. Ḩārat al-Wādī, which originally developed as a market (sūq, hence its other name, Ḩillat as-Sūq) along the low-lying southern edge of the oasis, eventually incorporated dwellings.

vra:description.source: Ministry of Heritage and Culture Sultanate of Oman, Birkat al-Mawz: Harat as-Saybani. Documentation and Heritage Management Plan, Masqaṭ: Mazoon Printing and Advertising L.L.C., 2014
